content: 1. Sulfamethoxazole and Diclofenac: Sulfamethoxazole may increase the levels or effects of diclofenac by altering the metabolism mediated by the hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear but considered minor. 2. Sulfamethoxazole and Diflunisal: Diflunisal can increase sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 3. Sulfamethoxazole and Digoxin: Sulfamethoxazole may elevate digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora and through competition for renal tubular clearance. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Close monitoring is recommended. 4. Sulfamethoxazole and Diltiazem: Sulfamethoxazole may increase diltiazem levels via competition for renal tubular clearance. The significance of this interaction is unclear but considered minor. 5. Sulfamethoxazole and Disopyramide: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 6. Sulfamethoxazole and Disulfiram: Disulfiram may increase sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 7. Sulfamethoxazole and Dofetilide: Sulfamethoxazole can increase dofetilide levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, necessitating close monitoring or therapy modification. 8. Sulfamethoxazole and Dolasetron: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 9. Sulfamethoxazole and Dosulepin: Sulfamethoxazole may decrease dosulepin levels through an unspecified mechanism. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 10. Sulfamethoxazole and Doxepin: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole may also decrease doxepin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Close monitoring is recommended. 11. Sulfamethoxazole and Dronabinol: Sulfamethoxazole may increase dronabinol levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Dronabinol is a substrate of CYP2C9. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Sulfamethoxazole and Dronedarone: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 13. Sulfamethoxazole and Droperidol: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Sulfamethoxazole and Drospirenone: Drospirenone may increase sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 15. Sulfamethoxazole and Efavirenz: Efavirenz may increase sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Sulfamethoxazole and Eltrombopag: Sulfamethoxazole may increase eltrombopag levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Sulfamethoxazole and Eluxadoline: Sulfamethoxazole may increase eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is advised when co-administered with strong CYP2C9/10 inhibitors. 18. Sulfamethoxazole and Enoxaparin: Sulfamethoxazole may increase the effects of enoxaparin by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 19. Sulfamethoxazole and Epinephrine: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 20. Sulfamethoxazole and Erdafitinib: Sulfamethoxazole may increase erdafitinib levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug used. If co-administration is unavoidable, close monitoring for adverse reactions and dose adjustments are necessary. 21. Sulfamethoxazole and Erythromycin (various forms): Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Sulfamethoxazole and Estradiol: Sulfamethoxazole may decrease estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and poses a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Sulfamethoxazole and Ethinyl Estradiol: Similar to estradiol, sulfamethoxazole may decrease ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms and poses a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Sulfamethoxazole and Ethotoin: Sulfamethoxazole may increase ethotoin levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism and decreasing its metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 25. Sulfamethoxazole and Etravirine: Sulfamethoxazole and etravirine may increase each other's levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 26. Sulfamethoxazole and Felbamate: Felbamate may increase sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 27. Sulfamethoxazole and Hydrochlorothiazide: Sulfamethoxazole may increase hydrochlorothiazide levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. Hydrochlorothiazide may also increase sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. There is a risk of hyponatremia. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 48. Sulfamethoxazole and Ibuprofen: Sulfamethoxazole may increase ibuprofen levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 49. Sulfamethoxazole and Ibutinide: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 50. Sulfamethoxazole and Iloperidone: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Sulfamethoxazole and Imidapril: Sulfamethoxazole and imidapril may interact through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia. Close monitoring is recommended. 53. Sulfamethoxazole and Lamivudine: Sulfamethoxazole may increase lamivudine levels by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 62. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but individual therapeutic response should be monitored to determine losartan dosage. 71.
